### REG-Q-071 — the durable turn record's `role` and `kind` are unconstrained strings that accept `''`,
no guard anywhere reads them, and the only vocabulary in existence is an app-side list whose `role`
values canon's ratified actor vocabulary does not contain — so what should type them is unsettled

**Date:** 2026-08-23 · **Type:** QUESTION (harmonization "Refuted (32)" re-disposition) ·
**Status:** OPEN

- **THE DEFECT, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, AND WHY IT IS A QUESTION AND NOT A FINDING.** `ConversationEntry` —
  the entire durable record of an authoring turn — types its two discriminators as bare
  `z.string()`: `role` and `kind` (`packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:189-190`). Driven, the
  contract accepts `role: ''`, `kind: ''`, and arbitrary junk in either. No guard anywhere in
  `rph-application` or `rph-domain` reads either field. So the durable record's own discriminators are
  whatever the untrusted producer said they were, which PER-10 forbids. **The gap is real; what is
  NOT settled is what should type them**, and that is why this is a QUESTION. Two plausible answers
  point in opposite directions, and writing a guard for the one the app already implements would
  ratify the narrower one by accident: the app's de-facto `role` values are `USER` / `AGENT` /
  `SYSTEM`, and **two of those three are not members of the ratified actor vocabulary at all.**

- **WHAT THE ARTIFACT REQUIRES, QUOTED VERBATIM.**
  - **JPWB-DOC-003 PER-10 · *Untrusted until admitted*** (`docs/canon/JPWB-DOC-003 Semantic Model and
    Invariant Catalog.md:373`): *"All inbound data — user input, model output, validator output, tool
    output, imports, templates, migration data, external API responses — crosses the full trust
    pipeline (parse, structural validation, normalization, **semantic validation**, authorization,
    conversion to domain values) before touching canonical state. Model output is untrusted external
    input; the system's own agents have no privileged bypass."*
  - **The Guide §9.4 "Envelope and schema rules"** (heading at `docs/Janumi Canonical Implementation
    Context - Coding Agent Guide.md:1230`), the wire rule at `:1238`: *"uppercase snake-case enums;"*.
    ⚠ **This cuts both ways and is part of the question.** The app's de-facto kinds are `message`,
    `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `error` — **lower-case**. Either they are enums and are spelled
    against `:1238`, or they are not enums and there is no vocabulary at all. Both readings are
    defects; they have different remedies.
  - **The ratified alternative the repository already ships.** `ActorReferenceSchema`
    (`packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:23-31`) — `actorId`, `actorType`, `displayName`,
    `roleId?`, `modelId?`, `providerId?`, `executionInstanceId?` — is REQUIRED on the object envelope
    as `createdBy`/`updatedBy` (`envelopes.ts:57`/`:59`) and on the event envelope as `actor`
    (`:150`), and its `actorType` is the ratified `ActorTypeSchema` enum
    (`packages/rph-contracts/src/enums.ts:7-14`): `HUMAN`, `AGENT`, `MODEL`, `SERVICE`,
    `POLICY_ENGINE`, `EXTERNAL_SYSTEM`. **`USER` and `SYSTEM` are not in it.**

- **WHAT THE CODE DOES, re-read at the sites at HEAD** (856dd8e1 — not a4a19057, which is now
  HEAD~1; the single commit between them touches only `docs/` and `verif/`, no site cited here).
  - `packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:188-193` — `ConversationEntrySchema = z.strictObject({ role:
    z.string(), kind: z.string(), text: z.string(), success: z.boolean().optional() })`. Neither
    discriminator is narrowed; `z.string()` with no `.min(1)`, no `.enum`, no refinement.
  - **The app-side vocabulary.** `apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/agent/transcript.ts:16-22`
    `TRANSCRIPT_KIND` maps five producer events to five kind labels, and `:25`
    `const RECORDABLE = new Set(['message', 'tool_call', 'tool_result', 'error'])` narrows the
    durable set to four (`thinking` is excluded by design under PER-12). It is a plain
    `Record<string, string>` and a plain `Set` — nothing generated, nothing ratified, nothing the
    schema imports.
  - **⚠ AND IT IS NOT THE ONLY ONE. A SECOND VOCABULARY EXISTS INSIDE THE CONTRACT'S OWN GENERATOR
    INPUT, CARRIED AS PROSE NOTHING CAN ENFORCE.** `objects.ts:1-2` declares the file generated from
    `vocab/m1-object-fields.json`; that file declares this sub-type at
    `packages/rph-contracts/vocab/m1-object-fields.json:3013` and gives BOTH discriminators a written
    vocabulary in a `note`: `:3019` *"USER | AGENT | SYSTEM — who produced this entry."* and `:3025`
    *"Render/semantic kind: message | thinking | tool_call | tool_result | error."* The generator
    emits neither — `objects.ts:188-193` carries no comment and no enum — so the vocabulary is
    **written down in the ratified-shape source and enforced nowhere**. **This sharpens the question
    rather than answering it:** the two written vocabularies already DISAGREE (the vocab note lists
    **five** kinds including `thinking`; the app's `RECORDABLE` admits **four**), and the vocab note
    is the artifact that enshrines `USER`/`SYSTEM` — the two labels `ActorTypeSchema` does not have.
  - **The `role` labels are string literals in one route file.** `USER` at
    `apps/rph-demo/src/routes/pwa/[id]/agent/+server.ts:304`, `AGENT` at `:195`/`:198`/`:204`,
    `SYSTEM` at `:112`/`:119`/`:141`/`:172`/`:182`/`:210`/`:329`. Eleven literals, three values, no
    declaration.
  - **The consumer depends on both untyped fields, and its fallback is silent corruption.**
    `apps/rph-demo/src/routes/pwa/[id]/+page.server.ts:64-77` `toLogEntry` switches on `e.kind`
    (`:66` `case 'message'` … ) and branches on `e.role === 'USER'` at `:67`; its `default:` at `:74`
    returns `{ kind: 'error', text: e.text }`. **So an unrecognized `kind` is not rejected — it is
    RENDERED TO THE PROFESSIONAL AS AN ERROR ROW**, and a producer typo becomes a false error in the
    permanent transcript with nothing anywhere reporting it.

- **OBSERVED — I DROVE THE CONTRACT.** Node against the built contract
  (`packages/rph-contracts/dist/objects.js:96`, byte-identical to `src` and newer; `src` clean at
  HEAD). Verbatim tool output:
  ```
  E role = arbitrary junk string  -> ACCEPTED
  F kind = arbitrary junk string  -> ACCEPTED
  G role = empty string           -> ACCEPTED
  H kind = empty string           -> ACCEPTED
  CONTROL missing text            -> REFUSED | invalid_type:text:Invalid input: expected string,
                                               received undefined
  ```
  **The control is what makes E-H mean something:** the schema is alive and does refuse a bad field,
  so accepting `''` for both discriminators is a decision the contract makes, not a dead parse.

- **OBSERVED, SECOND ROUTE — DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL COMMAND PIPELINE, not the schema in isolation.**
  A throwaway vitest suite over `Engine` + `SqliteStorageAdapter` (the harness at
  `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwa-authoring.test.ts:25-49`) dispatched a real
  `AppendConversationEntries` per case. Verbatim:
  ```
  A baseline {role,kind,text} -> ACCEPTED
  E role = junk               -> ACCEPTED
  F kind = junk               -> ACCEPTED
  G role = empty string       -> ACCEPTED
  H kind = empty string       -> ACCEPTED
  CONTROL missing text        -> VALIDATION_FAILED | RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED | Schema validation failed
  ```
  So an empty or arbitrary discriminator is not merely accepted by the schema — the **whole command
  is ACCEPTED by `Engine.dispatch`** against a real `SqliteStorageAdapter`, past parse, structural
  validation, authorization, and the DWP-08 precondition. ⚠ **EM-2, DISCLOSED AGAINST MYSELF:**
  the first two runs of this drive
  reported `A baseline -> REJECTED`, i.e. a DEAD CONTROL — a 25-char ULID made every case fail on the
  id rather than on the entry. The rows above are from the run whose control is ACCEPTED.

- **AND NO GUARD DOWNSTREAM CATCHES IT — DERIVED, NOT ENUMERATED.** The only precondition registered
  for `AppendConversationEntries` is `entriesNonEmpty`
  (`packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwa-authoring.ts:59-68`, JAN-CMDPRE DWP-08), whose message
  at `:65` is *"AppendConversationEntries changes nothing: the entries batch is empty…"* — a
  cardinality check, not a vocabulary one. `grep -rn "kind ===\|role ===" packages/rph-application/src
  packages/rph-domain/src --include=*.ts` (non-test) → **12 hits, and not one is a ConversationEntry**:
  `enforcement-register.ts` **7** (register-row kinds, `:3922`-`:4139`), `transition-gate.ts` **4**
  (`:443`/`:445` verdict kinds, `:820`/`:821` action kinds), and `conformance-manifest.ts:312`, which
  is a comment. **The grep form returns 12, so the instrument works and the absence is real** — and
  `packages/rph-application/src` contributes **0** of the 12, which is the half that matters here.

- **THE QUESTION, IN THE FORM AN ADJUDICATION CAN ANSWER.**
  1. **Is `role` on a conversation entry a label, or is it the ratified `ActorReference`?** If it is
     the ratified carrier, the remedy is to replace the string with `ActorReferenceSchema` — which
     would also make `modelId`/`providerId` sayable, and is the shape the object and event envelopes
     already require. If it is a label, which vocabulary — and does `USER`/`SYSTEM` stand, or does it
     become `HUMAN`/`SERVICE` to match `ActorTypeSchema`?
  2. **Is `kind` a ratified vocabulary, and if so which — and does the generator note become it?**
     Canon names none: `AUTHORING_CONVERSATION` appears in the corpus only as an object-type list
     member (`docs/canon/JPWB-SPEC-001 Professional Projection and Workbench Surface.md:8936`), and
     `packages/rph-contracts/src/enums.ts` declares **78** `z.enum`s of which **0** name a
     conversation kind or a turn role. The one written list is the generator note at
     `vocab/m1-object-fields.json:3025`, which is **five** kinds, not the app's four — so adopting it
     is itself a decision, not a transcription.
  3. **Does the answer to (2) settle `thinking` at the contract layer?** The app excludes `thinking`
     from `RECORDABLE` by rule (`transcript.ts:25`, docblock at `:14-15`); an enum omitting it would
     move that rule from a runtime filter into the contract. **That is REG-F-249's live subject
     (`:16909`) and must not be settled as a side effect of typing this field.**
  4. **What happens to entries already persisted with an unlisted `kind`?** PER-8 forbids hard delete
     after participation; an upcaster or a lifecycle disposition is required, not a migration that
     rewrites events (Guide `:1242`: *"persisted Events are immutable and permanent; schema change
     uses new versions/upcasters, never event rewrite"*).

- **⚠ WHY A GUARD WRITTEN TODAY WOULD RATIFY THE NARROWER READING.** The lists available to someone
  implementing now are the app's (three `role` literals, four `RECORDABLE` kinds) and the generator
  note's (the same three roles, but **five** kinds) — and they disagree. Encoding
  those as `z.enum` would (a) enshrine `USER` and `SYSTEM`, two labels the ratified actor vocabulary
  does not contain, (b) foreclose answer 1's `ActorReference` option by making the string field
  officially a label, (c) ship lower-case members against Guide `:1238`, and (d) settle `thinking` at
  the contract layer while REG-F-249 is open. **All four are decisions, and none of them has been
  made.** That is why this is filed as a QUESTION rather than as a `CODE_DIVERGES` finding with a
  remedy.

- **EM-7 SEARCH DISCLOSED, by id and by SITE, across all four corpora — Bash `grep`, long hits opened

### REG-Q-072 — an Assurance Observation cannot say WHEN it was observed: does PER-11's "where their
distinction matters" reach the observation, and if it does, is the observed time a fact about the
recording act or one a professional may declare?

**Date:** 2026-08-23 · **Type:** QUESTION · **Status:** OPEN

- **⚠ ADJUDICATION GATES THE CODE, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS NOT FILED AS A FINDING.** The engine already
  implements one of the two available readings — the observation's only times are the envelope's
  record-keeping stamps, so the observed moment is *de facto* the recording moment. **Two opposite
  remedies are available, each closes the gap, and each is a different ratification:** removing nothing
  and declaring the dimensions provably coincident, or adding a caller-settable observed time and with
  it the backdating hazard `REG-F-020` and `REG-F-014` name. Writing a guard for either would settle the
  canon question by accident, in code, with no act. **This is filed on `REG-Q-055`'s stated precedent,
  and distinguished from `REG-F-219`'s below.**

- **THE FACTS ARE NOT IN DOUBT; ONLY THE OBLIGATION IS.** What follows is established, driven where it
  could be driven. It is the *"where their distinction matters"* clause that needs an answer.

- **WHAT CANON SAYS, QUOTED VERBATIM.** `docs/canon/JPWB-DOC-003 Semantic Model and Invariant
  Catalog.md:377`, PER-11, under the heading `## 9. Persistence semantics` read off `:333` (not
  inferred), byte-exact: *"**PER-11 · Time is bitemporal; occurrence and record never conflate.** Every
  durable semantic record preserves semantic-occurrence time and record time as distinct meanings, and
  carries observed, valid, and Decision-effective time where their distinction matters. Exact field
  spellings and placement are repository shapes."*
  - **⚠ AND CANON'S OWN OBJECT ROW FOR THIS OBJECT NAMES NO TIME AT ALL**, which is half the question.
    Ratified canon gives the object no row of its own: `JPWB-DOC-003:93`, in `## 3. Core objects and
    minimum rules` (heading read off `:75`), is a COMBINED row, byte-exact —
    `| **Assurance Assessment / Observation** | Version-bound evaluation of Claims under an Assurance
    Policy; what was detected and its professional implication. Observation, interpretation, and Claim
    remain separate. |` (**`grep -c "Assurance Observation"` over DOC-003 → 0; controls in the same
    file: `Assurance Assessment` → 3, `Confidence Assessment` → 1, `Evidence` → 12.**) The Guide's
    §5.2 row, `docs/Janumi Canonical Implementation Context - Coding Agent Guide.md:389`, likewise:
    *"| **Assurance Observation** | What was detected or measured and its professional implication. …"*
    **Neither enumerates a time duty**, so the whole obligation — if there is one — rests on PER-11's
    general clause, and that is precisely the clause with a judgment condition in it.

- **WHAT THE CODE DOES, re-read at the site at HEAD.**
  - **THE OBJECT.** `packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:576-589`,
    `export const AssuranceObservationSchema = z.strictObject({ ...objectEnvelopeShape, assessmentId,
    policyId, criterionId?, subjectObjectIds, findingCode, observationType, severity, statement,
    implication, evidenceIds, disposition })`. Because it is a **`strictObject`**, no unlisted time
    field is even admissible — the gap is *inexpressible*, not merely unused. ⚠ **AND THE ONE OPEN
    CARRIER DOES NOT RESCUE IT:** the envelope's `extensions` array could in principle hold a time, but
    `RecordAssuranceObservationPayloadSchema` has no `extensions` key either (enumerated below), so a
    caller cannot supply one by that route.
  - **THE ENVELOPE.** `packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:49-65` — `objectEnvelopeShape` (the
    `ObjectEnvelopeSchema` built from it follows at `:67-68`) carries `createdAt` and `updatedAt` and no
    other time. `ProvenanceRecordSchema` (`envelopes.ts:35-42`) is `{ originType, sourceObjectIds,
    sourceEventIds, producingExecutionAttemptId?, producingValidatorId?, contentHash? }` — **no
    timestamp**.
  - **NEITHER WIRE SURFACE ADDS ONE.** Command: `packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:352-359`,
    `RecordAssuranceObservationPayloadSchema` = `{ assessmentId, observationType, findingCode?,
    severity, statement, evidenceIds? }` — **a professional cannot DECLARE when the thing was
    observed.** Event: `packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:938-949`,
    `AssuranceObservationRecordedPayloadSchema` = `{ observationId, assessmentId, policyId,
    subjectObjectIds, findingCode, severity, statement, implication, evidenceIds, disposition }` — no
    time field.

- **OBSERVED — DRIVEN for the shapes, READ for the canon.** The three key sets were **enumerated by
  `node` off the built contracts** (`packages/rph-contracts/dist/index.js`), not eyeballed:
  - OBJECT → `[id, objectType, schemaVersion, semanticVersion, revision, lifecycleStatus, createdAt,
    createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy, provenance, ontologyId, ontologyVersion, tags, extensions,
    assessmentId, policyId, criterionId, subjectObjectIds, findingCode, observationType, severity,
    statement, implication, evidenceIds, disposition]` — no observed or valid time.
  - COMMAND → `[assessmentId, observationType, findingCode, severity, statement, evidenceIds]`.
  - EVENT → `[observationId, assessmentId, policyId, subjectObjectIds, findingCode, severity,
    statement, implication, evidenceIds, disposition]`.
  - **CONTROL on the same instrument:** `AssuranceAssessmentSchema` enumerated the same way DOES carry
    `startedAt` and `completedAt`. The instrument reports time fields where they exist. Second control:
    the object schema REFUSES an unlisted key (`{observedAt: …}` → `false`), so `strictObject` is doing
    what this entry says it does.
  - **SECOND ROUTE, DIFFERENT ARTIFACT AND DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT:** the GENERATED JSON Schema
    `packages/rph-contracts/schemas/objects/AssuranceObservation.json`, parsed with `python`, declares
    exactly those 26 properties, `"additionalProperties": false`, and 23 `required` — **no observed and
    no valid time**, reached without the TypeScript build.

- **⚠ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE STRUCK ITEM'S WORDING, which do not touch its substance.** (1) The envelope
  carries `createdAt` **and** `updatedAt`, not *"only the envelope's createdAt"*. (2) The
  `AssuranceObservationRecorded` **event** envelope does carry two times — `occurredAt` and `recordedAt`
  are both REQUIRED at `packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:148-149`. But those are PER-11's
  **occurrence/record** pair, a different dimension from the **observed** and **valid** times at issue,
  and REG-Q-055 records that conjunct as already *"ENFORCED BY CONSTRUCTION"* via `makeEvent`.

- **THE VOCABULARY EXISTS IN THIS PACKAGE AND WAS SIMPLY NOT GIVEN TO THIS OBJECT — with a census and a
  positive control.** `grep -rnoE "observedAt|occurredAt|validFrom|validUntil|observationTime|
  detectedAt|effectiveAt|capturedAt"` over `packages/rph-contracts/src/*.ts` → **16 hits, all opened,
  none on this object**: `validFrom`/`validUntil` at `objects.ts:148-149` (`AuthorityReference`),
  `objects.ts:518-519` and `messages.ts:1188-1189` (Evidence); `capturedAt` at `objects.ts:517`,
  `messages.ts:194`, `messages.ts:1187`; `effectiveAt` at `objects.ts:603`, `messages.ts:371, 1101,
  1112, 1631`; `occurredAt` at `envelopes.ts:148` and `envelopes.test.ts:154`. **`observedAt` → 0.**
  **CONTROL on the same files and instrument:** `createdAt` → present in `objects.ts` and
  `envelopes.ts`; the alternation itself returns 16, so the zero for `observedAt` is a real absence.
  - **THE SIBLING OBJECT IS THE SHARP COMPARISON.** `EvidenceObjectSchema` (`objects.ts:508-521`), sixty
    lines above, carries `limitations` (`:516`), **`capturedAt` (`:517`, REQUIRED)**, `validFrom`
    (`:518`) and `validUntil` (`:519`) — and `capturedAt` is **caller-settable**, declared REQUIRED on
    `ProposeEvidencePayloadSchema` (`messages.ts:194`). **The engine already knows how to let a
    professional declare when something was observed. It gives that affordance to Evidence and not to
    Observation.** Whether that asymmetry is a defect or a correct reading of *"where their distinction
    matters"* is exactly the question.

- **⚠ HONEST NARROWING — NOTHING UPSTREAM IS BEING DISCARDED.** The gap is uniform through the stack, so
  this is not a case of a known time being dropped: `RecordableObservation`
  (`packages/rph-assurance/src/recording.ts:22-27`, fields at `:24-26`) is `{ code, severity,
  statement }` — the validator layer that feeds observations carries no observed time either. **A remedy
  would have to introduce the value, not merely stop losing it**, which raises the provenance question
  in the sub-question below.

- **THE CONFLICT, STATED AS A CONFLICT.**
  - **Canon reads one way.** PER-11 requires a durable record to carry **observed** time *"where their
    distinction matters"*, and an assurance observation is by definition *"what was detected or
    measured"* — a detection has a moment. A scan run last night and recorded this morning, a
    measurement taken against a build that has since moved, a finding transcribed from an external
    report: in each the observed moment and the record moment differ, and the engine cannot say so.
  - **The repository's own shape reads the other way.** Observations are minted only inside an
    assessment, by `recordAssuranceObservation`, from a validator result produced during that
    assessment — so the two dimensions **provably coincide** for every observation the engine can
    currently create. REG-Q-055 records that canon's own NON-EXAMPLE *"licenses omitting a field whose
    dimensions provably coincide"* (REG-005:`11496-11498`; the NON-EXAMPLE itself is `DOC-003:379`). On
    that reading the answer is *"it does not matter, for observations"*, and the correct outcome is a
    **recorded declaration of coincidence**, not a field.
  - **AND THE PRECEDENT CUTS BOTH WAYS.** `REG-F-020` (heading REG-005:**725**; the bullet at **:753**)
    deleted `GrantWaiver.effectiveAt` rather than honour it, reasoning that the moment a governance act
    became effective is *"a fact about the ACT"* and that honouring a caller-supplied value *"would
    permit a waiver to be BACKDATED — the manufacture-a-governance-fact shape REG-F-014 records."* An
    observed time a caller may set is that same shape, on the object that carries a blocking finding.

- **THE QUESTION.** **Is PER-11's *"where their distinction matters"* answered YES for
  `ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION` — (i) NO, because every observation the engine can mint is detected inside the
  assessment that records it, in which case the coincidence should be DECLARED (a site disclosure plus a
  guard-ledger row disposed `NOT_A_COMMAND_REFUSAL`), not left as a silent absence; or (ii) YES, in
  which case `AssuranceObservationSchema` and `RecordAssuranceObservationPayloadSchema` must gain an
  observed time?** Sub-question, because it is where REG-F-020's reasoning bites: **if (ii), is the
  observed time caller-DECLARABLE or engine-STAMPED — and if declarable, must a value disagreeing with
  the recording act be REFUSED rather than silently preferred, per REG-F-017, given that the validator
  layer supplies no such value today and a caller would be its only source?** Second sub-question:
  **does a validity window (`validFrom`/`validUntil`) belong on an observation at all, or is an
  observation's validity wholly derived from the Evidence it cites?**

- **⚠ IT WAS RECORDED AS REFUTED.** `docs/_working/HARMONIZATION-FINDINGS.md` item **#10** (line **98**),
  struck under the heading at line **87**, *"Refuted (32) — recorded so they are not re-raised"* (that

### REG-Q-073 — RATIFICATION: §7.3 declares TWO independent profile axes and forbids collapsing them, and
`Undertaking` carries ONE unconstrained string for both — the two PRODUCTION writers already disagree, and
neither of their values resolves against anything

**Date:** 2026-08-23 · **Type:** QUESTION (harmonization "Refuted (32)" re-disposition) · **Status:** OPEN

- **THE QUESTION, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** Guide §7.3 is titled *"Two independent profile axes"* and opens by
  forbidding their conflation. It defines two closed sets: an assurance/conformance **rigor** axis
  (Lightweight / Standard / High Assurance) and a **Product Realization work-shape** axis (Exploratory
  Product Shape / Feature Delivery Shape / Brownfield Change Shape / Migration Shape / High-Assurance
  Shape). `Undertaking` has exactly one profile-shaped field, `instantiationProfile`, typed `z.string()`
  with no enumeration, and no ratified text anywhere names that field and maps it to either set. So the
  question is prior to any binding: **which axis does this field carry, and where does the other one
  live?** It is not academic. The two PRODUCTION writers have already answered differently — one writes
  `'Standard Product Realization'`, a string built from a token of the rigor set and the qualifier §7.3
  attaches to the work-shape set; the other writes `'Standard'` — and **neither resolves against the only
  profile vocabulary that exists in code.** The work-shape axis has no carrier at all: none of its five
  members appears anywhere in the repository. **The collapse §7.3 forbids is not a mistake someone made;
  it is what the schema shape currently requires.**

- **WHAT THE ARTIFACT REQUIRES, QUOTED VERBATIM.**
  - **Guide §7.3 "Two independent profile axes"** — heading verified byte-exact at **L673** via
    `grep -n "^### 7\.3"`, NOT inferred from a line number. **L675**: *"Do not collapse assurance rigor
    into work shape."* **L677**: *"**Assurance/conformance rigor**"*, whose table header at **L679** is
    *"| Profile | Use and minimum consequence |"* with rows **Lightweight** (**L681**), **Standard**
    (**L682**) and **High Assurance** (**L683**). **L685**: *"**Product Realization work-shape
    profiles**"*, its members at **L687-691**: *"Exploratory Product Shape; Feature Delivery Shape;
    Brownfield Change Shape; Migration Shape; High-Assurance Shape."*
  - **`docs/Recursive Professional Harness/Janumi Professional Workbench PWA Designer and Undertaking
    Workbench - Reference Demonstration.md` §23 "Undertaking-to-PWA binding"** (heading at **L833**),
    item at **L839**: *"instantiation profile;"* — the source of the field's NAME, listing it among what
    every Undertaking records, **and supplying no vocabulary for it.**
  - **NOTHING IN CANON SETTLES IT EITHER WAY.** `instantiationProfile` appears in `docs/canon/` **20**
    times, all in REG-005 and all resolved below; the field appears in no canon vocabulary as a defined
    term, and no entry rules that it is deliberately free-form. **This is not moot-by-canon; it is
    unadjudicated.**

- **WHAT THE CODE DOES, re-read at the site at HEAD (`856dd8e1`), every line opened with `sed -n`.**
  - **UNCONSTRAINED AT ALL THREE LAYERS.** `packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:758`, inside
    `UndertakingSchema` (a `z.strictObject` at `:752`): `instantiationProfile: z.string(),`.
    `packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:649`, inside `CreateUndertakingPayloadSchema` (`:643`):
    `instantiationProfile: z.string(),`. `packages/rph-contracts/schemas/objects/Undertaking.json:247-249`
    is `"instantiationProfile": { "type": "string" }`, and `:286` lists it in `"required"`.
  - **AND THE ABSENCE OF AN `enum` IS REAL, NOT A GENERATOR LIMITATION — THE CONTROL IS IN THE SAME
    FILE.** `Undertaking.json:259-266` emits `"status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ACTIVE", "MIGRATING",
    "ARCHIVED"] }`. The generator DOES emit enums for constrained fields; it was simply told nothing here.
  - **THE ANNOTATION THAT DRIVES GENERATION IS EMPTY OF MEANING.**
    `packages/rph-contracts/vocab/m1-object-fields.json:1432-1436` carries exactly
    `{ "field": "instantiationProfile", "type": "string", "required": true }` — no enum, no note, no
    source citation — and `vocab/m3-commands-events.json:2726-2728` says the same for the command payload.
    **The gap is upstream of the schema, in the vocabulary itself.**
  - **THE §7.3 WORK-SHAPE SET EXISTS NOWHERE IN CODE.** `grep -rn "Exploratory Product Shape|Feature
    Delivery Shape|Brownfield Change Shape|Migration Shape|High-Assurance Shape"` (alternation, one
    `grep -E`) over `--include=*.ts --include=*.svelte packages apps`, non-dist → **0**. **POSITIVE
    CONTROL, identical command form and tree:** `HIGH_ASSURANCE` → **11**.
  - **THE ONLY PROFILE VOCABULARY THAT DOES EXIST IS A THIRD ONE.**
    `packages/rph-product-realization-pwa/src/ontology.data.ts:3603-3647` ships three
    `conformanceProfiles` keyed `LIGHTWEIGHT` / `STANDARD` / `HIGH_ASSURANCE`, resolved by
    `ontology.ts:44` `getConformanceProfile(name)`, whose only caller repository-wide is its own unit test
    (`ontology.test.ts:82`).
  - **THE TWO PRODUCTION WRITERS DISAGREE, AND A TEST ADDS A THIRD SPELLING.**

    `instantiationProfile: 'Standard',`; `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/disclosure-observed.
    test.ts:1867` → `instantiationProfile: 'STANDARD',`. Full census at HEAD, `grep -rn
    "instantiationProfile" --include=*.ts --include=*.svelte --include=*.json packages apps` (non-dist,
    non-`.svelte-kit`) → **19** lines: 2 Zod declarations, 2 JSON-schema lines, 2 vocab annotations, 1

## W-3b — the two artifacts the census still owed

Two entries closing what the invariant census recorded as outstanding after its arm doubts were settled.

**The RECORD correction** supersedes ONE bullet of `REG-F-234` and nothing else. That entry's finding —
the SUPPORTS endpoint pair at two command surfaces — is untouched and is not re-opened. What is corrected
is a clause describing a SIBLING ROW'S CENSUS BOOKKEEPING, which was **true when written** and has been
falsified twice since: once when V-7 filed that row, and again when its arm moved on an adjudicated doubt.

> ⚠ **An append-only entry that asserts another row's census bookkeeping makes a claim with an expiry
> date, in an artifact whose own `changeProcedure` forbids correcting it in place.** Cite a sibling's
> SUBSTANCE — the mechanism, the site — not its arm word or its filing status. Where the bookkeeping is
> genuinely load-bearing for a distinction, date it.

**The ratification question** is `limb:LYR-3:1`'s, and it is a question rather than a finding because
canon splits on it. Following `JPWB-DOC-003`'s provenance sidecar to the operative source: **five passages
fix LYR-3's subject by the canvas ACT** (*"Canvas layout operations must never increment semantic
version"*, *"Moving a node cannot alter a PWU semantic version"*) while **one fixes it by the EFFECT**
(Property P8, *"For ARBITRARY layout changes…"*). And the SCOPE line's own phrase is sharper evidence than
either: **`view-state` occurs exactly ONCE in the entire operative corpus**, where it modifies
*contracts*, not operations — so the operation-class framing is a canon-drafting transformation of a
corpus rule about contract SEPARATION. That seam is precisely where the question sits.

Both entries were adversarially verified and both were amended.

What presents here as an ARM RE-SCORING is therefore that migration renaming the pre-split value `superseded_verdict` carries, on a row REG-F-273 traced through every revision of `invariant-verdicts.ndjson` as unmoved since `2dff1d42`: REG-Q-053's clause was true when written, and REG-F-273 records it as not falsified at that entry's own reading of that ledger — so the defect is once again a quoted token compared against a mutable ledger rather than any misreading of one. **Nothing else in this bullet is disturbed:** this entry's finding — that an append-only artifact must not assert a mutable ledger's value — stands and is strengthened by REG-F-273, which corrects only its example and re-opens no finding. This entry is not edited, per §1.
  - **THE DISCIPLINE PROPOSED — cite a sibling's SUBSTANCE, not its bookkeeping; and where the

    sentence disposing of a sibling limb: (i) distinguish rows by **mechanism, file and field** — the

    — *"`filing: NEAR_MISS` as at 2026-08-21 (`invariant-verdicts.ndjson`)"* — so a later reader sees a
    timestamped reading rather than a standing claim; (iii) **never distinguish two entries by a phrase
    that describes an arm**, since arms are exactly what refuters move. ⚠ The trap in (i) is that an

- **THE FORM I FOLLOWED, AND ⚠ THE TENSION IN THE REGISTER'S OWN PRACTICE, RECORDED RATHER THAN
  SMOOTHED.** Two conventions exist and they are not the same act.
  1. **`changeProcedure` (line 19):** *"Entries are never destructively edited; a correction is a

### REG-Q-074 — RATIFICATION: is an ORDER-ONLY edit to `permittedChildTypeIds` a presentation operation

**Date:** 2026-08-23 · **Type:** QUESTION (W-3b invariant census, `limb:LYR-3:1`) · **Status:** OPEN

- **THE QUESTION, IN ONE SENTENCE.** LYR-3's SCOPE governs *"canvas/layout/view-state operations and
  their contracts"* — does that reach an edit to a field on a **semantic aggregate** whose ORDER no
  semantic consumer reads and whose only production order-consumers are presentation, so that a pure
  **order-only** change to `PwuType.permittedChildTypeIds` counts as a *"presentation operation"* for
  limb 1?

- **WHAT CANON SAYS, byte-exact at HEAD `73d1ec9e`.** `docs/canon/JPWB-DOC-003 Semantic Model and
  Invariant Catalog.md` **L71**: *"**LYR-3 · Presentation is meaning-inert.** No presentation operation
  may change semantic state or increment a semantic version. Layout has its own revision plane. No
  presentation contract may reference a Command capable of mutating PWU semantic state."* **L72**:
  *"if moving a node can change meaning, meaning becomes unauditable and untestable."* **L73**:
  *"**SCOPE:** governs canvas/layout/view-state operations and their contracts. **NON-EXAMPLE:**
  persisting layout and versioning it on its own presentation-revision axis is required, not forbidden
  — the rule bars *semantic* effect, not persistence."*

- **⚠ WHY CANON CANNOT ANSWER IT — THE SOURCE SPLITS ON EXACTLY THIS LINE, AND THE SPLIT IS REAL.**
  Followed under REG-D-034 from the sidecar to the extracts to the operative documents, each opened at
  its own line with `sed -n`. `JPWB-DOC-003 … .provenance.md:17` names LYR-3's sources verbatim:
  *"extract-doc002-b.md (RPH Canonical Domain Model L2148); extract-doc007-a.md (RPH-DOC-007 L160-164);
  extract-doc007-b.md (Contract Package L2322); extract-doc008-b.md (L2011-2018, Property P8
  L2346-2348). NON-EXAMPLE: NEW (P6)."*
  - **FIXING THE SUBJECT BY THE ACT AND ITS ORIGIN — five passages.** *Canonical Domain Model* **:2155**
    heading *"### No semantic mutation from presentation"*, **:2157** *"Canvas layout operations must
    never increment semantic version."* · *Contract Package* **:160** *"## 2.7 Presentation is
    non-semantic"*, **:164** *"Moving a node cannot alter a PWU semantic version."* · same file
    **:2322** *"No canvas-layout schema may reference a command capable of mutating PWU semantic
    state."* · *Conformance Spec* **:2011** *"## RPH-PRJ-004 — Layout change updates presentation
    only"*, **:2013-2018** *"Moving a node: updates presentation revision; does not change semantic
    version; emits no PWU semantic event; does not invalidate assurance."*
  - **FIXING IT BY THE EFFECT, NOT THE ACT — one passage.** *Conformance Spec* **:2346** *"## Property
    P8 — Presentation independence"*, **:2348** *"For arbitrary layout changes, semantic object
    versions and assurance states remain unchanged."* The quantifier is the opposite of a narrowing.
  - **⚠ AND THE SCOPE LINE'S OPERATIVE WORD IS A DRAFTING TRANSFORMATION, WHICH IS THE SHARP FORM OF
    THE SPLIT.** `view-state` occurs **exactly once** in the entire operative corpus — *Contract
    Package* **:162**, *"Canvas layout and view-state **contracts** must remain separate from semantic
    object contracts."* There it modifies **contracts**; canon's SCOPE line re-casts it as an
    **operation class**. The exact phrase *"view-state operation"* → **0** in the corpus. **POSITIVE
    CONTROLS, identical instrument and population:** *"Moving a node"* → **2**, *"presentation
    revision"* → **2**. (*"revision plane"* → **0**, so canon's L71 clause is itself non-corpus, and
    the sidecar independently marks the NON-EXAMPLE half of L73 *"NEW (P6)"*.)
  - **THE QUESTION IS THEREFORE PRIOR TO ANY VERDICT:** does LYR-3 bind by where an act **originates**
    (the canvas) or by what an act **is** (an operation whose only effect is view-state)? The
    arrangement below falls on opposite sides of that line, and no ratified text picks a side.

- **THE MEASUREMENT ALREADY MADE — WHAT MAKES THIS ANSWERABLE RATHER THAN ACADEMIC.** Every production
  consumer of `permittedChildTypeIds` was classified ORDER vs MEMBERSHIP, and **no governed consumer's
  OUTCOME turns on ORDER** — narrowed at HEAD from *"not one reads ORDER"*, which the surface site
  below falsifies. Census re-run at HEAD: **85** source lines across **17** files
  (`--include=*.ts --include=*.svelte` over `packages apps`, less `node_modules`, `dist`,
  `.svelte-kit`, `*.test.ts`, `e2e/`).

- **⚠ RE-VERIFIED AT HEAD, NOT CARRIED ON TRUST — a representative sample, DRIVEN with `node`.** Driver
  in the session scratchpad (`av_lyr3.mjs`, `av_lyr3b.mjs`, `av_lyr3c.mjs`, `av_lyr3d.mjs`), against
  the built `dist` of `@janumipwb/rph-projections`; these projections are pure, so better-sqlite3 is
  not involved. Arrangement: one root permitting four children, reversed **in order only**, membership
  identical.
  - **THE SEMANTIC-PATH ORDER-READER.** `packages/rph-projections/src/composition-plan.ts:113` —
    `planComposition`'s `for (const childTypeId of node.permittedChildTypeIds)`. Under reversal:
    `decompositions` **byte-identical**; parent→child relation identical
    (`ROOT->C1, ROOT->C2, ROOT->C3, ROOT->C4`); typeId multiset identical. **The tree is isomorphic.**
  - **⚠ THREE REFINEMENTS THE PRIOR RECORD DID NOT STATE, AND THEY DISCHARGE THEMSELVES.** `instances`,
    `offered` and `unresolved` are **NOT** byte-identical in general — **all three permute with the
    field.** On this arrangement `offered` and `unresolved` are **EMPTY both ways**, so a byte-identity
    claimed for those two here is **vacuous**; driven non-vacuously they move. Re-driven at HEAD: with
    two `C1`-cardinality children `offered` reverses; with two unresolvable permitted ids `unresolved`
    reverses; `instances`' plan-local keys permute (`i2`→`C1` forward, `i2`→`C4` reversed). **Only
    `decompositions` is order-inert, and the ISOMORPHISM is what the arm rests on.** None of the three
    is a semantic difference — each is equal AS A SET, and `composition-plan.ts:40` declares `key`
    *"a plan-local handle, not an id"*. Recorded so the next reader who drives this is not surprised by
    a `false` and reads it as a defect.
  - **THE GRAPH PROJECTION.** `buildPwaGraphExport` → `analyzePwaGraph` (`pwa-graph.ts:168`, `:378`;
    `collectPermits` declared `:132`, its order walk `:135`): `report.invariants` **byte-identical**,

    authored edge sequence differs and nothing reads it. `leafKind` (`leaf.ts:24`) → `NON_LEAF` both,
    reading `.length` only.
  - **MEMBERSHIP-ONLY CONSUMERS confirmed by reading the site:** `lint.ts:52` (`.filter(…)` then
    `.length`), `lint.ts:102` (`permitted.add(c)` into a `Set`), `pwa-graph-report.ts:49`
    (`.length === 0`), `pwa-authoring.ts:283` (`.length`).
  - **⚠ THE ONE PRODUCTION SITE THAT DOES CONSUME THE PLAN'S SEQUENCE — this narrows the census claim.**
    `apps/rph-demo/src/routes/undertakings/+page.server.ts` reads `plan.instances` IN ORDER at `:198`
    (`pwuIdByKey`, minting through `mintUiId` — a monotonic sequence, `workbench.ts:361`) and at `:201`

    commands, and WHICH unresolved pair the refusal names — while changing no tree, no gate outcome and
    no version. Read the census as *"no governed OUTCOME turns on order"*, never as *"nothing reads it"*.
  - **⚠ THE DISCRIMINATING POSITIVE CONTROL — and it takes TWO arrangements, not one.** ⚠ The prior
    record claimed a single membership change moved all four probes; re-driven at HEAD, **no single one
    does.** (A) one permitted id dropped, its node KEPT → `report.valid` **true → false**, `invariants`
    differ (`connected`: *"1 orphan(s): C4"*), permits set differs, and `unresolved` does **not** move.
    (B) the node removed, the permit KEPT → `unresolved` moves from `[]` to one `ROOT → C4` pair, while

- **WHAT TURNS ON THE ANSWER.**
  - **If YES** — an order-only edit is a presentation operation — then **limb 1 has a live subject and
    the arm is wrong.** The arrangement is dispatchable today: `EditPwuType` is accepted (its DWP-08
    no-op precondition compares with `isDeepStrictEqual` at `command-precondition.ts:100`, which is

  - **If NO** — the subject is fixed by the canvas act — then the arrangement is **OBJ-2 limb 5's**,

    `limb:OBJ-2:2`."* — **`limb:LYR-3:1` is deliberately absent**, and REG-F-209's cross-reference

## The register's own drafting habit, measured

`REG-F-272` corrected one clause that asserted a sibling row's census bookkeeping. This entry is the
general form it asked for — and it supersedes a clause of REG-F-272 itself, because that entry's tenth
example was misdiagnosed.

⚠ **REG-F-272 warned against exactly the mistake the first draft of this entry made.** At `:25136-25139`
it says *"No exact partition is asserted here; an entry that needs one must re-derive it and publish its
splitter."* The first draft asserted a per-batch table of 76 anyway. Two independently written extractors
then returned 41, 71, 109, 137 and 53 for the same corpus — **the number is a function of the scope rule
and nothing else** — and every limb-id-anchored count is an **undercount by construction**, because
entries name siblings in shorthand (`limb:DEC-4:1`, `:2` and `:6`) that no such extractor can see.

**The denominator is withdrawn. The numerator is eight, each read at its line and verified against the
census at HEAD.**

    `<commit>`"* — so a later reader knows to re-check rather than to trust.

### REG-F-274 — the register's own append-only rule has never had an instrument, and 26 in-place rewrites
of live entry text landed under it — including twice on the entry REG-F-273 cites as proof that cannot happen

- **Date:** 2026-08-27 · **Type:** DIVERGENCE FINDING (RECORD) · **Class:** RECORD — supersedes ONE CLAUSE

Coverage limit closed by **REG-F-280**. Date clause superseded by **REG-F-278**. ⚠ **The `70e4f33b` correcting entry this status previously advertised as *still owed* was FILED 2026-08-28 as `REG-F-282`** — the clause stood false for one day and is recorded in the census at **REG-F-284**.

- **THE DEFECT.** This register's `changeProcedure` (`:19`) reads *"Append-only after ratification … Entries
  are never destructively edited; a correction is a superseding entry citing the entry it supersedes."*
  **Nothing has ever checked it.** Adjudicated over 71 commits by five readers and five adversarial
  verifiers: **26 confirmed in-place rewrites of live entry text**, the first landing **2026-08-02 — nine
  days after REG-D-010 ratified this register** — and running to 2026-08-21. They cluster on `**Status:**`
  and `**Merge target:**`, the two most load-bearing fields an OPEN entry has.

- **⚠ THE SANCTIONED IDIOM EXISTS AND IS THE EXCEPTION.** Retiring text by striking it (`~~old~~` plus an
  appended replacement, as at `:57`) preserves everything. **9 lines carry a struck `~~**Status:**` against
  445 carrying `Status:`.** Four of the 26 commits apply the strike correctly *in the same hunk* as a
  violation, so this is **selective application, not ignorance of the idiom** — and why it is selective is
  not known and is not claimed.

- **⚠⚠ THE KEYSTONE, AND IT IS REG-F-273'S OWN CITED EXAMPLE.** That entry names **`REG-F-072:2255`** as
  proof of a stale claim sitting uncorrectable in an append-only artifact — its census figures
  `UNENFORCED 44 · ARROW_UNREACHABLE 22 · ENFORCED 14 · REDUNDANT_WITH_MACHINE 2`, false at HEAD against
  `verif/guard-enforcement-ledger.test.ts:59-62` which pins **42 / 20 / 18 / 2**. **That entry's
  Merge-target/Status line was destructively rewritten IN PLACE TWICE ON 2026-08-08** — by `8cfc341b`, then
  by `174047b8` — **and `174047b8` is the commit that authored the stale figures in the same hunk.**
  > **The register rewrote that entry's BOOKKEEPING twice in one day and left its SUBSTANCE to rot for
  > nineteen days.** The correction mechanism was available, was used twice on that exact line, and still
  > did not reach the claim.

- **WHAT THIS DOES TO REG-F-273 — THE PREMISE FALLS, THE REMEDY IS STRENGTHENED.** Read normatively its
  clause is true: the rule does say entries are never destructively edited. Read as a DESCRIPTION of the
  artifact — which is what makes the harm bite — it is **false**. The remedy survives on three grounds:
  (1) the in-place edits **do not reach the stale claims**, which the keystone proves on the entry's own
  example; (2) an audit record is read **at revisions**, and in-place correction does nothing for any reader
  before it; (3) the in-place edits **are themselves the defect** — a remedy repaired by pointing at them
  would license `c61d92cf`, which erased a live fourteen-document obligation, and `fb5d7cbd`, which erased a
  standing ratchet still true when deleted. **The reason is restated as the measured one: the register
  corrects its status lines in place and its substance never.**

- **⚠ NO RATE IS PUBLISHED, PER REG-F-272 `:25136`.** Two independent splitters move the candidate
  population — the history traversal (`--no-merges` = 298 commits; `-m --first-parent` = 200) and the
  line-eligibility rule — and they move it comparably. Three defensible derivations give **103, 106, 130,
  131 and 163**. **The published figure is a RANGE, 103–163, and no member of it is "the" number.** The
  adjudicated **26 of 71 is a FLOOR, not a total**: the readers answered about the candidate lines they were
  handed rather than each commit's full diff, so `fb5d7cbd` rewrote four entry lines not three, `29b14912`
  five not two, and `d4be2574` was graded *"nothing removed"* while deleting `REG-F-020`'s Status line.
  **That batching defect was the commissioning agent's, and it is recorded rather than absorbed.**

- **THE INSTRUMENT.** `verif/register-append-only.test.ts` — an entry-scoped unigram word-count contract
  against the register at a pinned commit, with a whole-file count absolving a word that merely relocated.
  **The two obvious designs were built and REJECTED BY MEASUREMENT:** a history assertion over git deletions
  flags 6 of 9 compliant strikes; an n-gram shingle contract flags 12 of 12, because re-wrapping destroys
  every n-gram. **Driven, not predicted:** the forbidden act (a live line rewritten in place, on disk)
  **REDDENS**, naming `REG-F-049: lost ["COMPLETE","at","audit","corrected",…]`; the sanctioned act (the
  same line struck and replaced) **STAYS GREEN**; and the fail-closed path **fired on the first run**, on a
  real bug — `git show <rev>:<path>` resolves from the repository root, and this package is a subdirectory.
  ⚠ **The green mutant is what makes this a control rather than a tripwire**: without it, "the gate
  reddened" would prove only that it reacts to edits, not that it tells the forbidden act from the permitted
  one. **No grandfather list is needed** — the baseline pins the current state, so the 26 are absorbed and
  the gate guards forward only. **Coverage limit, stated as a limit:** a rewrite that deletes a word and
  re-adds it elsewhere *within the same entry* passes; bigram strengthening would close that, was not
  measured, and is therefore not claimed.

- **THE 26 ARE NOT SWEPT.** Rewriting them would be a large unreviewed edit to the audit record — the
  argument `verif/register-status.test.ts:74` already accepted when it grandfathered 63 entries BY ID.
  Append a one-line pointer to each affected bullet instead. **Prioritise by truth at removal:** four
  removed text still TRUE AND LIVE (`c61d92cf`, `fb5d7cbd`, `5fd041f3`, `574cc1e6`); **`70e4f33b` needs a
  correcting entry regardless**, because a sentence still standing at `:560` says a prescription *"is kept
  unstruck because it was right"* while the same commit deleted half of it — **false about this register's
  own history**; the remainder removed a claim the removing commit had itself just falsified.
  ⚠ **`git log -S` is the wrong instrument for that sweep** and would hide the keystone: the `REG-F-072`

- **THE DEFECT.** `REG-F-272:25182` states that `REG-F-040` reached its disposition *"having found that **no

  `REG-F-105` (`:3055`), `REG-F-106` (`:3090`), `REG-F-108` (`:3142`). `REG-F-272` was written **2026-08-23**

  is not the original finding but its UNDATED REPETITION**, in the present perfect, as though it were a
  standing property rather than a measurement with a date.

- **⚠⚠ AND THIS IS WHY REG-F-273'S RULE IS RIGHT AND ITS SCOPE IS TOO NARROW.** That rule names *a sibling
  row's CENSUS BOOKKEEPING*. **This is not census bookkeeping.** It is a **finding about this register's own
  state** — exactly as mutable, and mutable by the very acts `REG-F-274` records. **`REG-F-273` generalised

- **WHAT THIS DISCHARGES.** `REG-F-274` records 26 confirmed in-place rewrites of live entry text and
  prescribes, deliberately in place of a sweep: *"Append a one-line pointer to each affected bullet
  instead."* **28 pointers over 22 entries were authored, adversarially verified, and are recorded below.**

- **⚠⚠ AND THE PRESCRIBED FORM WAS PERFORMED, MEASURED, AND REVERTED — IT COSTS MORE THAN IT REPAIRS.**
  The 28 pointers were applied to the bullets exactly as prescribed. Applying them inserts 34 lines into the
  body of the register at 28 sites between `:473` and `:3309`, **and every line-number citation below an
  insertion moves.** Measured on the artifact, not estimated:
  - **594** line-number citations matched in the register; **543** sit at or below the first insertion and
    therefore shift — **364 of them by 34 lines.**
  - The strictly verifiable subset — citations of the form `` `REG-x-nnn:NNNN` `` whose target can be tested
    against that entry's own line span — is **17, and all 17 land inside the entry they name at HEAD.**
    **The convention is maintained and reliable, which is exactly why breaking it is expensive.**
  - **This register cannot repair them.** A stale line citation inside an append-only artifact is permanent.
  **So the pointers were reverted from the body and re-issued here, where they shift nothing.** The register
  is back to 17/17 and the citations are intact.

- **⚠ THE APPENDIX FORM ALSO PRESERVES THE INSTRUMENT, WHICH THE IN-BULLET FORM WAS ERODING.**
  `verif/register-append-only.test.ts` absolves a lost word when it reappears in an entry that existed at the
  baseline. **An in-bullet pointer quotes the very text the destructive edit removed, into the very entry
  that lost it** — so the annotation systematically re-supplies the words the gate is watching for.
  Driven: with the in-bullet pointers applied, the gate's forbidden-act mutant fell from naming **nine** lost
  words to **one**, and a second attempt keyed on the commit hash `3f70bcfe` fell to **zero**, because the
  annotation quoted the hash too. **`REG-F-274`'s remedy was eroding `REG-F-274`'s gate.** A NEW entry cannot
  absolve — the gate counts "elsewhere" only over baseline-existing entries — so the appendix form is the one
  that leaves the instrument at full strength. The gate's mutants now DERIVE a once-only token at run time
  and fail loudly if none exists, rather than trusting a hard-coded one twice invalidated in a day.

- **WHAT IS LOST BY THE APPENDIX FORM, STATED PLAINLY.** `REG-F-273` argued for the in-bullet form because
  *"a superseding entry with no pointer never reaches the reader it exists to protect."* **That cost is
  real and is accepted here**: a reader who opens `REG-F-049` and reads only that entry will not see this.
  The trade was 28 co-located pointers against 543 permanently stale citations plus a degraded gate, and it
  was made on measurement. Every annotation below names its entry id, so a reader who greps the entry id —
  the same act that finds any superseding entry in this register — finds it.

### REG-F-278 — REG-F-274's date range is wrong: the destructive-edit practice is a nine-day burst that
STOPPED on 2026-08-10, and this correction is an append because that entry's own subject forbids the edit

- **Date:** 2026-08-27 · **Type:** DIVERGENCE FINDING (RECORD) · **Class:** RECORD — supersedes ONE CLAUSE
  of **REG-F-274**, filed earlier the same day
- ~~**Status:** OPEN~~
- **Status:** **MERGED 2026-08-28 AS TO THE RE-DERIVATION RULE.** Carried by `JPWB-DOC-004 §10 item 9` (v1.5.0). ⚠ It merged as a NEW item rather than an amendment to item 8, on the ground that **item 8's remedy cannot detect this defect**: a dated reading tells a reader when to re-check a value, and dating a figure that was already false when measured yields a dated false figure. Item 8 guards DECAY; item 9 guards TRANSCRIPTION.

- **THE CORRECTED FACT.** `REG-F-274` states the 26 confirmed in-place rewrites ran *"beginning 2026-08-02 …
  and running to 2026-08-21."* **The second date is false.** All 26 fall between **2026-08-02 and
  2026-08-10** — author date and committer date both, all 26 hashes resolved, none after 2026-08-10. The
  window opens nine days after `REG-D-010` ratified this register on 2026-07-24, and closes after **nine
  days**.

- **⚠ AND THE PRACTICE STOPPED — THE SAMPLE DID NOT MERELY THIN, WHICH IS THE CHECK THAT MAKES THIS A
  FINDING RATHER THAN AN ARTIFACT.** Nine candidate commits dated **2026-08-17, 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-21**
  were adjudicated in the same pass, and **none of the nine was destructive.** Later commits were looked at
  and came back clean; the absence after 2026-08-10 is measured, not unsampled.

- **HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, BECAUSE THE MECHANISM IS REUSABLE.** The analysis synthesis conflated the
  **CANDIDATE** range with the **CONFIRMED** range. `29b14912` (2026-08-21) is a candidate line-loss and is
  **not** among the 26; the candidate population is a superset extending eleven days further, and the
  sentence took its end date from the wrong set. *This is the same defect this programme has now filed three
  times: a scope is an answer to a question, and reusing it silently answers a different question.*

- **⚠⚠ AND IT IS THE THIRD CARRIED FIGURE IN TWO DAYS THAT WAS WRONG.** `REG-F-273` said four stale claims
  and it was eight; its per-batch denominator of 76 was withdrawn entirely; and now this date. **The common
  form is not arithmetic — it is a figure produced inside an agent's synthesis and then RESTATED BY THE
  ORCHESTRATOR WITHOUT BEING RE-DERIVED.** All three were caught by re-deriving from the primary artifact,
  none by re-reading the prose. **The rule that follows, and it is owed to the corpus: a figure that will be
  written into canon is re-derived at the point of writing, from the primary artifact, or it is not
  written.** This is `JPWB-DOC-004 §10 item 8`'s obligation pointed at the author rather than the reader.

- **A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE STOP, OFFERED AS ONE.** `REG-F-040` (2026-08-06) is titled *"WHY THIS IS AN ENTRY
  AND NOT AN EDIT"* — this register diagnosing the practice on itself, four days before the last instance.
  **Not tested; no causal claim is made.** It is recorded because the next agent to ask *why* it stopped
  should start there and should know it is unverified.

- **⚠ WHAT "STOPPED" DOES NOT CLAIM.** The candidate population is DERIVED: a removed line becomes a
  candidate only if its normalised text fails to reappear in the same commit and is absent at HEAD. **A
  destructive edit whose exact words happen to recur elsewhere never becomes a candidate at all.** So the
  claim is *no destructive edit was FOUND after 2026-08-10*, which is weaker than *none occurred*, and the
  difference is not measured.

- **⚠ THIS CORRECTION IS AN APPEND, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** `REG-F-274`'s subject is 26 entries corrected
  by overwriting. **Correcting it by overwriting would have been the twenty-seventh.**

- **WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED IN REG-F-274.** The count of 26; the floor-not-total caveat; the 103–163
  candidate range and its two splitters; the keystone (`REG-F-072` rewritten twice on 2026-08-08 by commits
  one of which authored the still-false census figures); the disposition of `REG-F-273`'s premise; and the
  gate. **Only the end date changes** — and it changes the finding's SHAPE, from a standing habit to a burst
  that ended, which is why it is filed rather than noted. **It raises the gate's value rather than lowering
  it:** a practice that stopped by informal means can resume by informal means, and until today nothing
  could have reported the relapse.

- **RECONCILIATION.** Closes no census limb. Supersedes the date clause of `REG-F-274` and nothing else.

- **Merge target:** **This register** (the correction) · **Corpus**, jointly with `REG-F-273/274/275`, for
  the re-derivation rule. Status: OPEN.

- **THE CORRECTED FACT.** `REG-F-276` states that **four** of the eleven `UNENFORCED_DEAD_PREDICATE` rows —

### REG-F-280 — the deferred bigram strengthening is REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, not deferred again: it reddens
the sanctioned act, and the register's own shape is what makes that unavoidable

- **Date:** 2026-08-27 · **Type:** DIVERGENCE FINDING (RECORD) · **Class:** RECORD — closes the R-5 open
  item of `DESIGN-register-append-only.md` · **Status:** CLOSED

- **THE OPEN ITEM.** `REG-F-274`'s gate carries a stated coverage limit: *"a rewrite that deletes a word and
  re-adds the same word elsewhere within the same entry … passes. Bigram strengthening would narrow it, was
  not measured, and is therefore not claimed."* **It is now measured.**

- **IT CLOSES THE HOLE.** Constructed adversary: delete a phrase from `REG-F-049`'s live line and re-add its
  six tokens **scrambled** as a new bullet in the same entry. Unigram flags **0**; bigram flags the entry
  and names the six lost pairs. The variant that re-adds them inside a *different* baseline entry is caught
  too. **Both halves of the stated limit close.**

- **⚠⚠ AND IT IS REFUTED ON COST, BY THE CONTROL THE GATE EXISTS TO PASS.** **MUTANT B — the SANCTIONED act,
  a line retired by `~~strike~~` plus a replacement — REDDENS**, under both tokenizations tried. Beyond it:
  - **7 of the 11** commit×entry pairs where the current gate correctly permits a real adjudicated compliant
    strike are converted to RED.
  - Over the **30** first-parent commits since 2026-08-11 — a window in which no destructive edit was found
    — unigram reddens 12 and bigram reddens 26. **In every one of the 14 extra, not a single WORD was lost;
    only adjacency was.**
  - **On real history the detection gain is zero:** over the 26 confirmed destructive commits, unigram flags
    26/26 and bigram flags 26/26, the same entry ids in every case.

- **THE MECHANISM, READ RATHER THAN INFERRED — AND IT IS THE REGISTER'S OWN SHAPE.** Two causes, both of them
  the sanctioned idiom: **(1) a strike destroys the bigrams at BOTH EDGES of the struck span**, which is why
  the previously-rejected shingle contract flagged 12 of 12 and why n=2 inherits it more quietly; **(2) an
  entry ends in a `Merge target:` / `Status:` trailer, so an APPEND INTO AN ENTRY LANDS MID-STREAM and severs
  one pair at the junction.** A bare bullet added above the trailer — nothing struck, nothing removed — goes
  RED. **That refutes the property that makes this gate survivable on an append-only artifact: that appends
  are free.**

- **NO TOKENIZATION ESCAPES IT, AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS ALSO REFUTED.** Entry-wide tokenization survives
  re-wrapping and dies on an interior append; per-line survives the append and dies on re-wrapping; **both
  die on MUTANT B.** The natural fix — report a lost bigram only when one of its words is also lost as a
  unigram — restores the strike and the append to green **and returns the constructed evasion to green too.
  It is the unigram gate with extra steps.**

- **THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT IS NOT THE RATE BUT WHAT GENERATES IT.** The false-positive rate does not merely
  persist; **it scales with normal use of the register, and it fires hardest on the two acts the rule exists
  to encourage — appending, and correcting by strike.** A gate that reddens when you obey it is a gate that
  gets disabled, which this programme has already recorded twice as how instruments die here.

- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** No claim that bigram has more false negatives (it caught 26/26 and no evasion
  defeating bigram-but-not-unigram was searched for). No claim about n > 2. **No claim for the alternative
  named below** — it is an untested hypothesis about code that does not exist, which is the status this
  programme assigns to a recorded remedy.

- **THE RESIDUAL HOLE STAYS OPEN AND STAYS STATED.** An author who deletes a phrase and re-adds its words
  scrambled within the same entry passes. **That is a deliberate reconstructive act, not a slip, and the
  instrument that would catch it costs more than the act it catches.** If it must be closed, the next thing
  to measure is **not n=3 but an insertion-tolerant order check** — a longest-common-subsequence over the
  entry's token stream, which is unaffected by pure insertion and would therefore pass the strike, the
  re-wrap and the append while still failing the evasion. **Not measured. Not claimed.**

- **⚠ THE DECISIVE CLAIM WAS RE-DRIVEN BY THE FILING AGENT, AND THE FIRST TWO ATTEMPTS FAILED TO REPRODUCE
  IT — WHICH SHARPENED THE MECHANISM.** Striking the **whole line** and appending a replacement is **GREEN**
  under bigram; so is a partial strike whose replacement lands where the tokens were not adjacent. The red
  appears only when the strike's boundary falls **between two previously adjacent tokens** — reproduced
  byte-exactly, `REG-F-049` losing `["at 3f70bcfe"]` when the struck span ends at `at` and the replacement
  lands before the hash, with unigram GREEN on the identical input. **So the claim is not "a strike reddens"
  but "a strike whose edge severs an adjacent pair reddens", which is precisely why the measured figure is 7
  of 11 and not 11 of 11.** Recorded because a reader who tests the easy case will conclude this entry is
  wrong: the first two reproductions here did.

- **RECONCILIATION.** Closes R-5 by measurement rather than leaving it as an untested *"would"*. The gate is
  unchanged; the design paper's coverage-limit sentence is superseded by this entry rather than rewritten.

- **Merge target:** **Repository** — no code change; `docs/_working/DESIGN-register-append-only.md` §7 records
  the measurement. Status: CLOSED.

### REG-F-281 — REG-F-273's six pointers are applied by INLINE EXTENSION, a third form that shifts nothing,
and REG-F-273 closes

- **Date:** 2026-08-28 · **Type:** DIVERGENCE FINDING (RECORD) · **Class:** RECORD — discharges
  **REG-F-273**'s own closure condition and refines the form rule of **REG-F-277**
- ~~**Status:** CLOSED~~
- **Status:** **CLOSED 2026-08-28.** `REG-F-273` closed on it, and its own corpus leg — the annotation form rule — is now carried by `JPWB-DOC-004 §10 item 10` (v1.5.0). Nothing remains owed.

- **WHAT THIS DISCHARGES.** `REG-F-273` has stood **MERGED as to its drafting rule, OPEN as to its own
  closure condition** since 2026-08-27: *"CLOSES when a one-line ⚠ SUPERSEDED IN PART pointer is appended at
  the END of the bullet holding each corrected clause … since a superseding entry with no pointer never
  reaches the reader it exists to protect."* **All six pointers are now applied.** The entry closes.

- **⚠ THE CLOSURE CONDITION NAMED "THE SIX SITES" AND LISTED FIVE.** `REG-F-273` supersedes one clause each
  of `REG-F-235`, `REG-F-237` and `REG-Q-062`, **two** of `REG-F-236`, **and one of `REG-F-272`** — six
  clauses over five entries. Its line list omits the `REG-F-272` one, which the entry names elsewhere, at
  `:25536`, as `REG-F-272:25141-25145`. **The sixth was located from the supersedes clause rather than the
  list**, and it is `REG-F-272`'s *"the tenth is not `NEAR_MISS`"*. A list that disagrees with its own count
  is a cheap defect to catch and was nearly missed.

- **⚠⚠ AND THE FORM IS A THIRD ONE, BECAUSE BOTH KNOWN FORMS ARE WRONG HERE.** `REG-F-277` faced the same
  question for 26 pointers and reverted the in-bullet form to an appendix, because inserting lines into the
  register's BODY moves every line citation below them. **Neither form is right for these six**, and a third
  was measured instead:

  | form | shifts citations | reaches the reader at the bullet |
  |---|---|---|
  | **A** — a new line inside the bullet (what `REG-F-273` literally prescribes) | **yes** | yes |
  | **B** — an appendix (what `REG-F-277` adopted for the 26) | no | **no** |
  | **C — INLINE EXTENSION: append to the END of the bullet's existing LAST LINE** | **no** | **yes** |

  **Form C satisfies `REG-F-273`'s condition literally — the pointer IS at the end of the bullet — while
  adding no line at all.** Driven: the register is 26,090 lines before and after; the set of indices whose
  content differs is exactly the six target lines, and **every other line is byte-identical at the same
  index**, so no citation anywhere in canon, code or `docs/_working` can go stale.

- **THE GREEN IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A VACUITY.** `verif/register-append-only.test.ts` passes under form C —
  and the positive control with a KNOWN-OPPOSITE expected value is the same six clauses **deleted outright**,
  which goes **RED naming all five entries**. So the instrument reacts to exactly these entries and form C's
  green discriminates. `verif/register-status.test.ts` likewise passes, with its own opposite control: the
  identical extension carrying a `Status:` token goes **RED**.

- **⚠ TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT TRAVEL WITH THIS FORM, AND THE SECOND CAME FROM A CONSUMER, NOT A GATE.**
  1. **The extended line must not carry `**Status:**`.** `scripts/tracker/ingest.ts:109` captures an entry's
     status with a regex that runs **to END OF LINE** — extending such a line would swallow the pointer into
     the tracker's recorded status. None of the six is such a line; the applier refuses one that is, and
     that refusal is exercised by its own control.
  2. **The pointer must carry no `Status:` token**, for the same reason. `REG-F-272` states the underlying
     rule at `:25199`: the register admits exactly one Status line per entry.

- **THE DISCLOSED COST, STATED BECAUSE IT IS REAL.** `git diff --numstat` scores form C as **6 added /
  6 deleted** — it rewrites six lines' bytes rather than adding six lines. **That is a history-legibility
  cost, not a content one**, and `git log -p` will show six modified lines rather than six pure additions.
  It is the same distinction the ratified instrument was built on: a git-deletion assertion flags 6 of 9
  adjudicated-compliant strikes and is the wrong instrument, which is why `verif/register-append-only.test.ts`
  measures content survival instead.

- **⚠ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF THAT COMMISSIONED THIS, BOTH DOWNWARD.** (1) The orchestrator estimated
  **117** register-internal citations would move under form A; an independent extractor could not reproduce
  that figure under any of four definitions and returned **223 minimum**. That is a claim about two
  extractors and not a refutation of either — but it moves in the direction that makes form A worse, so it
  does not change the trade. **No single figure is published; the range is 117–223 and the splitter is the
  extraction rule.** (2) The brief said **14** of the 17 verifiable citations move under form A. It is
  **13**: `REG-F-235:12528-12534` targets a line ABOVE its own bullet-end at `:12537`, and at the placement
  `REG-F-273` actually prescribes — the END of the bullet — it does not move.

- **RECONCILIATION.** Closes `REG-F-273` in full. Refines `REG-F-277`'s form rule from *"annotate at the end
  of an append-only artifact"* to **"an annotation must not move existing line numbers; where the bullet's
  last line can carry it, extend that line, and only otherwise use an appendix."** Does not re-open
  `REG-F-235`, `REG-F-236`, `REG-F-237`, `REG-Q-062` or `REG-F-272`, whose findings and closures are
  untouched — each pointer says so in terms.

- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** Form C is not proposed for the 26 of `REG-F-277`: those were reverted for a
  measured reason and re-issuing them inline was not measured. **No claim that form C is free of every cost**
  — its git-legibility cost is stated above, and a line already at an unreasonable length would be a reason
  not to use it (none of these six is; they run 87–100 characters).

- **Merge target:** **This register** (the six pointers, applied) · **Corpus** for the refined form rule,
  which belongs with `JPWB-DOC-004 §10 item 8` as a drafting rule about annotating an append-only artifact.
  Status: CLOSED as to `REG-F-273`; the corpus merge of the form rule is OPEN. ⚠ **THAT MERGE LANDED 2026-08-28** as `JPWB-DOC-004 §10 item 10`; see the entry's bolded status below.

### REG-F-282 — `70e4f33b` deleted REG-F-012's prescription and wrote, in the same hunk, that it *"is kept
unstruck because it was right"*: a claim about striking, made by the hand that did not strike

- **Date:** 2026-08-28 · **Type:** DIVERGENCE FINDING (RECORD) · **Class:** RECORD — corrects one sentence
  standing in **REG-F-012**; discharges the correcting entry that `REG-F-274` named as owed regardless of
  the annotation sweep and that `REG-F-277` recorded as not discharged when it took the appendix form ·
  `**Status:**` OPEN

- **WHAT THE COMMIT DID, QUOTED FROM BOTH SIDES OF IT.** `70e4f33b` (2026-08-04 06:31:23 -0400) rewrote
  `REG-F-012`'s Disposition bullet in place, in one hunk. From the pre-image
  (`70e4f33b^:…/JPWB-REG-005 Decision and Divergence Register.md:550-551`) it **REMOVED** the whole of the
  prescription — *"The fix is small (compare `commandType`, `targetAggregateId` and a payload hash against
  the receipt before returning `DUPLICATE`; refuse on mismatch) but it is a **behaviour change that will
  refuse commands the engine accepts today**, so it takes the REG-F-011 treatment: a caller/fixture survey
  first, then a red-first test written against the CONTRACT — that a mismatched reuse is REFUSED with a
  classified code — rather than against a chosen error string. The refusal needs an error code;
  `RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` is **not** among the ratified fifteen, so this also inherits REG-F-010's
  question of whether to carry the label in the message (the WP-11 discipline) or ratify a code."* — and
  the whole of the line beneath it, *"**Merge target:** Repository — `command-bus.ts` (the comparison), and
  a probe. JPWB-DOC-003 §9 PER-5 is unchanged and correct: canon already states the rule. `**Status:**`
  OPEN."* In their place it **ADDED** *"~~Recorded, not fixed.~~ **FIXED 2026-08-04 for two of PER-5's
  three dimensions.** The prescription below was followed as written and is kept unstruck because it was
  right."*, followed by five sub-bullets reporting the work done.

- **⚠ THE ADDED SENTENCE IS FALSE — AND WHICH PART OF IT IS FALSE MATTERS, BECAUSE THE THREE CLAIMS IN IT
  DO NOT STAND OR FALL TOGETHER.**
  1. ***"was followed as written"* — a claim about the CODE, and it is TRUE.** All three comparisons the
     deleted clause prescribed are performed in one expression:
     `packages/rph-application/src/command-bus.ts:452-457` tests `prior.commandType`,
     `prior.targetAggregateId` and `prior.payloadHash` before answering from a receipt. **This limb is not
     the finding and is not disturbed.** It was false as to the payload dimension for the ninety-six
     minutes between this commit and `ac1a0274` — and the same bullet said so in its own next sentence,
     which is candour, not defect.
  2. ***"the prescription below"* — the deixis names nothing.** At the moment the sentence was written
     there was no prescription below it. The five sub-bullets it introduced are past-tense reports of
     completed work (*"THE SURVEY. Instrumented across the whole suite…"*, *"Red-first, with both controls
     already passing before the fix…"*); not one of them prescribes anything.
  3. ***"is kept unstruck"* — a claim about THIS REGISTER'S OWN TEXT, and it is false, was false as it was
     being written, and cannot become true.** The words it says were kept are not in the artifact. Nothing
     was struck. The text was deleted.

- **THE MEASUREMENT, AS A DATED READING OF THE RECORD THAT OWNS IT.** Read 2026-08-28 at `024b8c9c`,
  scoped to `REG-F-012`'s own span: `The fix is small (compare` = **0**, `REG-F-011 treatment` = **0**,
  `refuse on mismatch` = **0**, `and a probe` = **0**, `canon already states the rule:` = **0** — against
  firing controls **on the same instrument and the same span**, `REG-F-011` = **1** and
  `RPH_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` = **1**, both carried by the replacement text itself. ⚠ **A whole-file count
  does not settle this one and now reads the wrong way:** the first three phrases score **1** file-wide,
  all three on one line — `REG-F-277`'s appendix, which quotes them in order to correct them. Quoting is
  not asserting (`JPWB-DOC-004 §10 item 8`), so the entry-scoped count is the evidence. **The 2026-08-27
  reading moved the instrument it was taken with**, and that is recorded here so a later reader does not
  mistake the 1 for survival.

- **⚠⚠ AND THERE IS A SECOND PROOF THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WORD COUNTS AT ALL — A CROSS-REFERENCE LEFT
  POINTING AT NOTHING.** The sub-bullet this same commit added ends *"…carries `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` in
  the message — the WP-11 discipline **this entry named**"* (`REG-005:566` at `024b8c9c`). `WP-11` occurs
  **exactly once** in the entry, in that referring clause. In the pre-image it also occurred exactly once —
  **inside the deleted prescription**, which is where the entry named it. **The reference and its referent
  never coexisted: one hunk added the pointer and removed the thing pointed at.** This is what defeats the
  only serious defence the sentence has — that the surviving sub-bullets ARE the prescription, restated —
  because a restatement does not leave a cross-reference dangling.

- **⚠ THE IRONY IS THE FINDING, NOT A FLOURISH.** Measured over the one hunk: the added text contains
  **exactly one strike**, `~~Recorded, not fixed.~~`, preserving **three words**; the same hunk deleted
  **131** — 106 of prescription and 25 of Merge-target-and-Status.
  > **A claim that a text was left unstruck is itself a claim about striking, and this one was written by
  > the hand that, in the same hunk, struck three words and deleted a hundred and thirty-one.** The idiom
  > exists so that exactly this claim can be checked against the artifact instead of taken on the author's
  > word. Here it was applied to the three words that needed it least and withheld from the hundred that
  > carried the obligation — `REG-F-274`'s *"selective application, not ignorance of the idiom"*,
  > demonstrated by the very sentence that denies it.
